Time to play Filipino games. You're doing great!
Let's explore Filipino art and culture. You've got this!

sentences.text: Lola wakes up early every Saturday morning.
She goes to the wet market to buy fresh chicken and vegetables.
At home, she washes the chicken and cuts the vegetables.
She lights the clay stove and places the pot on top.
Soon, the water starts to boil.
Lola adds ginger, onion, and the chicken pieces.
The kitchen smells warm and delicious.
Her granddaughter Ana runs to the kitchen.
Lola, what are you cooking? Ana asks.
Tinola, my dear, Lola says with a smile.
She adds the vegetables and green leaves.
Ana gets a bowl and waits for lunch.

comprehension_questions.stem: When does Lola wake up early?
Where does Lola go to buy ingredients?
What does Lola buy at the wet market?
Where does Lola place the pot?
What does Lola add to the boiling water?
Who runs to the kitchen?
Why does Ana run to the kitchen?
comprehension_questions.correct: She is curious about the warm smell of food

comprehension_questions.stem: How do Lola and Ana feel about the tinola?
Why is tinola special to Ana?
comprehension_questions.correct: It is made with love by her Lola
distractors: It is a new recipe from the internet
It is her favorite restaurant dish
It is the cheapest food at the market

comprehension_questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
comprehension_questions.correct: A Lola cooking warm tinola for her granddaughter
distractors: A family going to the beach
A child learning to cook alone

sentences.text: Every summer, the children of Barangay Maligaya play outside all day.
They wake up early and meet at the plaza.
First, they play piko on the street.
Maria hops on one foot and balances carefully.
Your turn, Pedro! she says.
Then they play tumbang preso with an old tin can.
Pedro throws his slipper and hits the can.
Everyone cheers!
In the afternoon, the children fly a saranggola.
The kite soars high in the blue sky.
Some boys spin their trumpo on the ground.
Some girls jump over a rope and sing.
The games of our childhood are always fun.
When the sun sets, the children go home tired but happy.

comprehension_questions.stem: Where do the children of Barangay Maligaya play?
Where do the children meet?
What is the first game they play?
What does Maria do during the piko game?
What game do they play with a tin can?
What does Pedro throw at the tin can?
What do the children fly in the afternoon?
What do some boys spin on the ground?
How do the children feel while playing?
Why are these games called the games of our childhood?
comprehension_questions.correct: Filipino children have played them for many years
distractors: They are new games from other countries
They can only be played in school
They need expensive toys to play

comprehension_questions.stem: How does the writer show the children's happiness?
comprehension_questions.correct: By describing how they play and cheer together
distractors: By listing the rules of each game

comprehension_questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
comprehension_questions.correct: The joy of playing traditional Filipino games during summer

sentences.text: Lolo Mario was a famous artist in his town.
He painted beautiful pictures when he was young.
His studio is filled with art from long ago.
On the wall hangs a picture of an old arena.
It reminds him of the Spoliarium.
Beside it stands an old film projector.
Lolo used to show movies in their plaza.
Every night, the whole town would watch.
Now, his three grandchildren visit him every weekend.
Lisa, Ben, and Carla love to hear his stories.
Lolo, teach us how to paint, Lisa says.
Lolo smiles and gives each of them a brush.
Art is a gift of our people, he says.
We must never forget our culture.
The children paint bright suns on their paper.

comprehension_questions.stem: What was Lolo Mario known for in his town?
What did he paint when he was young?
What hangs on the wall of Lolo's studio?
comprehension_questions.correct: A picture of an old arena

comprehension_questions.stem: What does the picture remind Lolo of?
What stands beside the picture?
Where did Lolo use to show movies?
Who visits Lolo now?
What does Lisa ask Lolo to teach her?
Why does Lolo say art is a gift of our people?
comprehension_questions.correct: Because art belongs to our Filipino culture
distractors: Because art is easy to learn

comprehension_questions.stem: What does Lisa paint on her paper?
Why is it important to remember our culture?
comprehension_questions.correct: So that the traditions of our people will not be lost
distractors: So we can sell more paintings
So we can forget our history
So only Lolo will be famous

comprehension_questions.stem: Why did Lolo feel sad about the old film projector?
comprehension_questions.correct: Because fewer people watch movies in the plaza now
distractors: Because it is heavy to carry
Because it belongs to someone else

comprehension_questions.stem: What can you learn from Lolo and Lisa's story?
comprehension_questions.correct: We should pass on Filipino arts and culture to the next generation
distractors: Only old people can make art
Art is only for famous painters
Children should not learn from their elders

comprehension_questions.stem: Why do you think the author wrote this passage?
comprehension_questions.correct: To remind readers to value and continue Filipino art and culture
distractors: To teach readers how to build a projector
To describe a foreign film festival
To convince readers to leave their hometown
